hypotheses.latent_object: A contraction template T(K2, K3; a, b, c; orientation) with base two-index kernel K2_{mn} and three-index kernel K3_{mnl}, plus edge-labeled h factors.
hypotheses.construction_plan: Read K2 from S1 by factoring h1(b,n,m)*h2(a,c,m,n); then S2 is obtained by permuting external labels b and c while keeping K2 unchanged. Read K3 from S3 by factoring h1(a,m,n)*h1(b,ell,m)*h1(c,n,ell); then S4 is obtained by a permutation of the index arguments of the b and c h1-factors while keeping K3 unchanged.
required_assumptions: The two-index kernel K2 is symmetric under b<->c external label exchange.
The three-index kernel K3 is invariant under the stated edge-index permutation.
h1 and h2 are generic functions with no hidden relation to the kernel coefficients.
proof_obligations: Coefficient(Piecewise(S1), h1*h2) == Coefficient(Piecewise(S2), h1*h2) after b<->c
Coefficient(Piecewise(S3), h1*h1*h1) == Coefficient(Piecewise(S4), h1*h1*h1) after index permutation
All piecewise branch conditions are preserved by the permutation.
hypotheses.rationale: The piecewise polygamma coefficients are visually identical between S1 and S2 and between S3 and S4; only the external h1/h2 labels and argument order differ.

hypotheses.latent_object: A single two-index kernel F_{mn}(beta,gamma,mu,epsilon) that is the full polygamma coefficient in the S1/S2 summands.
hypotheses.construction_plan: Define F_{mn} as the coefficient multiplying h1*h2 in the first double sum. Reuse F_{mn} with different external labels in the second double sum.
required_assumptions: F_{mn} does not depend on the external labels a,b,c except through parameter and index positions.
The h functions are separate from F.
proof_obligations: F(S1)_mn - F(S2)_mn = 0 for each Piecewise branch
The only difference between S1 and S2 is the external label assignment in h1/h2.
hypotheses.rationale: The two double sums contain exactly the same Piecewise coefficient structure and differ only in the attached h-factor labels.

hypotheses.latent_object: A meromorphic base kernel L(x,y,z; beta,gamma,mu) such that the nonconfluent branches are divided differences of L in the epsilon variables, and the diagonal/confluent branches are derivative limits taken at coincident indices.

theta.confluent_cases: same as S3 under index permutation

hypotheses.construction_plan: For each branch, express the rational coefficients and polygamma(k) terms as divided differences or confluent limits of a base kernel L. Off-diagonal denominators (epsilon(i)-epsilon(j))^{-r} fix the divided-difference order r; confluence produces polygamma order equal to the number of coalescing variables.
required_assumptions: The base kernel L has poles with residues producing the observed polygamma(0) terms.
Coincident limits exist and match the Piecewise branches.
proof_obligations: Compute divided differences of L and compare with off-diagonal branch of S1
Compute confluent limits and compare with Eq(m,n) branch of S1
Repeat for S3/S4 triple-index branches including theta, ell=m, ell=n cases
hypotheses.rationale: The expression contains many denominators (epsilon(i)-epsilon(j))^r and polygamma orders aligned with coincidence depth, which is the signature of a confluent divided-difference expansion.

hypotheses.latent_object: A master function Psi(z)=polygamma(0,z), evaluated at arguments z=(beta*(gamma +- I*mu -+ I*epsilon(i)) + pi)/(2*pi); every polygamma(k) is d^k Psi/dz^k.
hypotheses.construction_plan: Replace polygamma(k, z) by d^k/dz^k polygamma(0,z) throughout the expression. This exposes the full expression as a differential polynomial in a single master function Psi.
required_assumptions: Psi is analytic in the needed region.
proof_obligations: For each k=0..4, verify polygamma(k,z)=d^k/dz^k polygamma(0,z)
Substituting the derivative identity leaves every piecewise branch unchanged.
hypotheses.rationale: All non-rational special functions are polygamma of integer order, so all transcendental parts are generated from polygamma(0) by differentiation.
